media.alt: Child health research making impact in Pakistan

content.text: Children are the nation's future and research into the health and well being of children is essential to secure a thriving and prosperous Pakistan, this was the key theme emerging from a research dissemination seminar held at Aga Khan University (AKU) on Friday and Saturday.

Organised under the aegis of AKU's Department of Paediatrics, the two-day event highlighted major accomplishments in documenting the burden of childhood disease in Pakistan and effective solutions for addressing them at multiple levels of the health system, from patient-based clinical care to population-based programs and national health policy.

In his message to the seminar participants, Secretary of Health, Sindh, Dr. Noshad Shaikh stressed the critical importance of children and child health for the future of our country. Acknowledging the efforts of the conference organisers Dr. Zulfiqar Bhutta (Professor and Chair of Paediatrics) and Dr. Anita Zaidi (Associate Professor Paediatrics), he said that the outcome of the research held special significance for Sindh province as the work was being done locally, in urban and peri-urban settlements as well as in the rural locations of Hala and Matiari. The Secretary offered the full cooperation of the provincial Ministry of Health in a partnership with different stakeholders directed towards improving the child health situation in the country.

In his opening remarks, AKU president Mr. Shamsh Kassim-Lakha H.I., S.I., lauded the efforts of AKU's child health research team, which had been working extensively on issues of global and national child health priorities for many years. He said that the quality and impact of the work could be judged by the interest displayed by international grants and donor agencies, including World Health Organisation (WHO) and United Nations Children Education Fund (UNICEF), as well as the Sindh and Federal Ministry of Health, Islamabad. Moreover, he noted, much of the work had been published in international scientific journals of repute, which highlighted the rigour and exemplary standards of the research, and provided an important measure of impact and dissemination.

AKU paediatrics faculty presented scientific talks. Investigators discussed a broad range of child health problems, including diarrhoeal illnesses, high incidence of stillbirths, low birth-weight babies, deaths in the newborn period, and unrecognised illnesses such as dengue and typhoid fevers.
